ring.title: Ring Cursor Effect — Smooth Follower Ring | Chase's CV
ring.description: Preview a smooth ring cursor that follows pointer movement with configurable size, color, border width, and easing.
ring.ogImageAlt: Ring cursor effect preview with adjustable size and smoothing
ring.behavior: Draws a ring that lerps toward the pointer. Smoothing controls how quickly the ring catches up; size and border width shape the halo.
ring.useCases: Product landing pages, portfolio heroes, and playful marketing sites that need a lightweight branded pointer without particle overhead.

params.size: size — outer diameter of the ring or lens

magnifier.title: Magnifier Cursor Effect — Lens Zoom Preview | Chase's CV
magnifier.description: Magnify content under the cursor with zoom, blur, brightness, and saturation controls plus the same ring smoothing as the ring effect.
magnifier.ogImageAlt: Magnifier cursor lens with zoom and smoothing controls
magnifier.behavior: Combines a following ring with a lens that zooms and stylizes pixels beneath the pointer. Lens blur, brightness, and saturation shape the glass look.
magnifier.useCases: Design showcases, before/after demos, and editorial layouts where you want users to inspect details under the cursor.

params.size: size — outer diameter of the ring or lens
params.lensBrightness: lensBrightness — brightness boost under the lens
params.lensSaturate: lensSaturate — saturation boost under the lens

trail.title: Trail Cursor Effect — Dot Trail Behind the Pointer | Chase's CV
trail.description: Leave a throttled trail of dots behind movement with controls for dot count, size, color, and emission interval.
trail.ogImageAlt: Trail cursor effect with configurable dot trail
trail.behavior: Spawns dots along the pointer path on a throttle timer. maxDots caps history length; size and color define each stamp.
trail.useCases: Playful brand sites, game promos, and interactive art pieces that reward movement with motion graphics.

params.maxDots: maxDots — maximum trail stamps kept alive
params.size: size — outer diameter of the ring or lens
params.throttleMs: throttleMs — minimum milliseconds between trail dots

spotlight.title: Spotlight Cursor Effect — Dimmed Stage with Pointer Hole | Chase's CV
spotlight.description: Darken the page except for a circular spotlight that follows the cursor, with radius and dim color controls.
spotlight.ogImageAlt: Spotlight cursor effect with dimmed overlay
spotlight.behavior: Applies a dim overlay with a circular cutout centered on the pointer. Radius sets the lit area; dimColor controls the surrounding shade.
spotlight.useCases: Guided tours, storytelling scroll experiences, and reveal moments that focus attention on one region at a time.

params.dimColor: dimColor — rgba overlay outside the spotlight

magnetic.title: Magnetic Cursor Effect — Attract Elements to the Pointer | Chase's CV
magnetic.description: Pull elements matching a CSS selector toward the cursor with adjustable strength and preview item color.
magnetic.ogImageAlt: Magnetic cursor effect attracting UI blocks
magnetic.behavior: Targets elements via selector (default [data-magnetic]) and offsets them toward the pointer based on strength. itemColor tints preview blocks.
magnetic.useCases: Button grids, card stacks, and micro-interaction demos where nearby UI should feel pulled toward the cursor.

params.selector: selector — CSS selector for magnetic targets
params.itemColor: itemColor — preview color for magnetic blocks

flame.title: Flame Cursor Effect — Rising Fire Particles | Chase's CV
flame.description: Emit rising flame particles from the pointer with controls for emission rate, size, lifetime, rise speed, jitter, and DPR cap.
flame.behavior: Spawns particles that rise and fade with jitter. emission sets spawn rate; lifeMs and rise shape motion; maxDpr limits canvas density.
flame.useCases: Seasonal campaigns, game launches, and high-energy hero sections that need fiery motion tied to the cursor.

params.emission: emission — particles spawned per frame batch
params.size: size — outer diameter of the ring or lens
params.jitter: jitter — random motion for flame particles
params.maxDpr: maxDpr — device pixel ratio cap for flame canvas

smoke.title: Smoke Cursor Effect — Drifting Smoke Particles | Chase's CV
smoke.description: Emit soft smoke puffs that rise and drift from the pointer with color, size, lifetime, and motion tuning.
smoke.behavior: Similar to flame but with slower rise and horizontal drift for wispy smoke. color tints each puff; emission and lifeMs control density.
smoke.useCases: Moody portfolios, music releases, and atmospheric landing pages that need subtle environmental motion.

params.emission: emission — particles spawned per frame batch
params.size: size — outer diameter of the ring or lens

invertRing.title: Invert Ring Cursor Effect — Blend-Mode Halo | Chase's CV
invertRing.description: Ring cursor that inverts or blends with the background using blend modes, optional blend background, and ring smoothing.
invertRing.ogImageAlt: Invert ring cursor with blend mode controls
invertRing.behavior: Renders a ring whose pixels interact with the page via CSS blend modes (default difference). blendBackground can force a backdrop color for predictable contrast.
invertRing.useCases: Bold typography heroes, poster-like layouts, and experiments where the cursor should cut through color blocks.

params.size: size — outer diameter of the ring or lens
params.blendMode: blendMode — CSS mix-blend-mode for invert ring
params.blendBackground: blendBackground — optional backdrop color behind the ring

electricArc.title: Electric Arc Cursor Effect — Click Bursts and Arcs | Chase's CV
electricArc.description: Spawn electric arcs around the pointer with length, radius, lifetime, glow, emission rate, and click burst tuning.
electricArc.ogImageAlt: Electric arc cursor effect with glow
electricArc.behavior: Draws short-lived arcs near the pointer. clickBurst adds extra arcs on click; glowColor softens the neon edge around color.
electricArc.useCases: Sci-fi product teasers, gaming UIs, and interactive posters that need energetic feedback on move and click.

params.emission: emission — particles spawned per frame batch
params.glowColor: glowColor — outer glow tint for arcs
params.clickBurst: clickBurst — extra arcs spawned on pointer down

landing.purposeBody: The Flow Editor is an experimental visual workspace for SFC-style structured flows. It renders the tree on a zoomable canvas, lets you add sequential steps or branches, and surfaces node properties in a side panel—useful when a JSON or YAML flow is too hard to hold in your head.
landing.step1: Load the demo flow and pan or zoom the canvas to orient yourself.
landing.step2: Select a node to inspect IDs, descriptions, and branch metadata in the properties panel.
landing.step3: Use the toolbar to add sequential steps, branches, or expand supported branch nodes.
landing.step4: Toggle runtime highlight to see how execution might travel through the current structure.
landing.useCase1: Sketch onboarding or approval flows before wiring them into production orchestration.
landing.useCase2: Explain branching logic to teammates without scrolling through nested config files.
landing.useCase3: Prototype how runtime highlighting could help operators debug stuck flows.

sfc.question: What kind of flows does it model?
sfc.answer: It focuses on structured, tree-shaped flows similar to SFC drafts: sequential steps, condition nodes, and explicit branches—not a general-purpose whiteboard.

edit.question: Can I import my own production flow?
edit.answer: Not in this playground release. The page ships with a demo tree so you can explore editing mechanics without connecting to a backend.

demo.question: What does runtime highlight show?
demo.answer: A illustrative pass over the demo graph so you can discuss execution order and branch joins—it's a visual aid, not a live production trace.

export.question: Can I export JSON or code?
export.answer: No export yet. The tool is for visualization and hands-on editing practice inside the browser session.

browser.question: Does it work on mobile?
browser.answer: The layout is responsive, but dense editing is most comfortable on a desktop-sized screen with a pointer.

landing.purposeBody: Image to UI is a browser-based color palette extractor for UI design. It pulls dominant colors from an uploaded image or curated painting sample, classifies them into surface, action, and support roles, and previews how the palette behaves in realistic SaaS layouts. Classic masterpieces remain built-in examples, but the workflow works for any image you bring.
landing.step1: Choose a sample painting or upload an image from your device.
landing.step2: Wait for the palette extraction to finish in your browser.
landing.step3: Select three colors to assign surface, action, and support roles.
landing.step4: Generate the interface preview and compare dashboard and landing layouts.
landing.useCase1: Turn brand photography or mood boards into a first-pass UI palette before coding.
landing.useCase2: Stress-test contrast and hierarchy when borrowing colors from art or nature references.
landing.useCase3: Explore theme direction quickly without exporting tokens or installing a design-system package.
landing.rolesIntro: Instead of listing raw hex values, the preview explains how each selected color is expected to behave in interface hierarchy.
landing.roleSurfaceBody: Backgrounds, cards, and large calm areas that carry most of the layout.
landing.roleActionBody: Primary buttons, links, and focus states that need readable contrast against surfaces.
landing.roleSupportBody: Borders, inputs, secondary labels, and muted accents that structure the UI without competing with actions.
landing.privacyBody: Uploaded images stay on your device. Palette extraction runs in the browser with client-side libraries, and this site does not receive your file contents or filenames for analytics.

upload.question: Can I use my own images?
upload.answer: Yes. Use the local upload control to pick JPG, PNG, or WebP files. Processing happens entirely in your browser.

server.question: Are images uploaded to a server?
server.answer: No. The tool reads the file locally to extract colors. Nothing is sent to Chase's servers for storage or analysis.

roles.question: What do surface, action, and support mean?
roles.answer: They are UI color roles: surfaces hold layout, actions drive primary interaction, and support colors handle borders, inputs, and secondary emphasis.

preview.question: What does the preview show?
preview.answer: A themed SaaS dashboard, settings panel, and marketing landing layout that demonstrate how your palette might feel in product UI—not production code.

export.question: Can I export or copy a full shadcn theme?
export.answer: Not yet. The current release focuses on extraction, role mapping, and visual preview. It does not generate installable theme files or copy-paste shadcn configuration.

landing.purposeBody: Dudu Scanner is a playful belly-scan console for family-friendly reveals. Pick a snack or creature theme, choose mystery or operator mode, tune sound, then run a fullscreen-friendly scan that ends in a goofy character cameo—entertainment only, not a medical device.
landing.step1: On the setup screen, choose a theme, scan mode, and optional sound.
landing.step2: Press start scan to enter the immersive view with keyboard shortcuts ready.
landing.step3: Sweep the probe (or let auto-scan run) until the signal is strong enough to lock.
landing.step4: Reveal the character, share the laugh, then reset for another round.
landing.useCase1: Turn a hidden stuffed animal or snack joke into a mini stage performance.
landing.useCase2: Let kids "operate" the scanner with printed shortcut cards before the big reveal.
landing.useCase3: Record a short clip of the scan UI as a playful pregnancy or party easter egg.

family.question: Is it safe for kids?
family.answer: It's a silly browser toy with gentle sound and cartoon characters. Always supervise young operators and remember it's entertainment—not health advice.

setup.question: What's the difference between mystery and operator mode?
setup.answer: Mystery mode secretly picks a character from your theme each round. Operator mode lets you lock in the exact character before the show starts.

sound.question: Can I mute the scanner?
sound.answer: Yes. Toggle sound on the setup screen or press M during a scan to silence effects.

fullscreen.question: Does fullscreen work on phones?
fullscreen.answer: Browsers vary. The UI offers a fullscreen retry shortcut, but the most reliable experience is landscape tablet or desktop.

surprise.question: Will it spoil a real surprise?
surprise.answer: Operator mode shows your pick up front. Use mystery mode when you want the audience to discover the character live.
